title: Therapeutic intranasal delivery of NanoSTING provides broad protection against seasonal and highly pathogenic influenza strains 2258688
abstract: Abstract Introduction Seasonal and highly pathogenic influenza strains pose major public health challenges. Broad-spectrum therapies that protect vulnerable populations, accelerate recovery, and reduce mortality are a long-sought goal for influenza. We developed NanoSTING, a liposomal formulation of 2’3’-cGAMP, the endogenous STING-activator, to activate mucosal innate immunity as a host-directed therapy. Methods NanoSTING stability was assessed by DLS, zeta potential, and HPLC. Pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), and safety were assessed in BALB/c mice after a single intranasal dose of NanoSTING. The nasal/lung tissues were analyzed by qPCR for IFN genes (Ifnb1 and Cxcl10) and by H&E for safety. To model vulnerable populations, we tested aged (18—20 mo), cyclophosphamide-lymphodepleted, and dexamethasone-treated (immune-suppressed) mice for NanoSTING-induced mucosal IFN responses, safety, and protection in viral challenge. Therapeutic efficacy was tested against influenza (A/H1N1pdm, B/Brisbane, and H5N1) challenge models. Results NanoSTING was stable for 12 months at 4oC with no loss of encapsulated cGAMP. A single intranasal dose induced robust Ifnb1 and Cxcl10 in nasal and lung tissues without histologic injury. In influenza A/H1N1 and B challenge models, one dose of NanoSTING reduced weight loss, accelerated recovery, and outperformed ten doses of oseltamivir. In models with highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI, H5N1), NanoSTING reduced viral titers and disease severity even when administered 48—72 h post-infection. NanoSTING-induced nasal innate immunity was preserved in lymphodepleted, dexamethasone-treated, and aged mice, supporting its use in vulnerable hosts. Conclusion Single-dose intranasal NanoSTING activates protective type I IFN programs and delivers broad therapeutic benefit across influenza A/B, including H5N1, with an extended treatment window, refrigeration stability, and dose-sparing administration—highlighting a cellular, host-directed path to durable respiratory antiviral defense. Funding Source NIH, AuraVax Topic Categories Mucosal and Regional Immunology (MUC)

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 季节性和高致病性流感毒株构成了重大的公共卫生挑战,保护弱势群体、加速康复和减少 死亡率 的广谱疗法是流感长期追求的目标。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在 BALB/c 小鼠中进行,包括老年(18-20 个月)、环磷酰胺淋巴细胞去除和地塞米松治疗(免疫抑制)小鼠,以模拟易感人群,并测试了针对流感(A/H1N1pdm、B/布里斯班和 H5N1)攻击模型的治疗效果。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 DLS、zeta 电位和 HPLC 评估 NanoSTING 稳定性;单次鼻内给药后评估药代动力学(PK)、药效学(PD)和安全性;通过 qPCR 分析鼻/肺组织中的 IFN 基因(Ifnb1 和 Cxcl10),并通过 H&E 分析安全性。
elements_zh.main_results: NanoSTING 在 4°C 下稳定 12 个月,封装的 cGAMP 没有损失;单次鼻内剂量在鼻和肺组织中诱导出强大的 Ifnb1 和 Cxcl10,而没有组织学损伤;在甲型/H1N1 和乙型流感攻击模型中,一剂 NanoSTING 减少了体重减轻,加速了恢复,并且优于十剂奥司他韦。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,单剂量鼻内 NanoSTING 可激活保护性 I 型 IFN 程序,并为 A/B 型流感(包括 H5N1)提供广泛的治疗益处,具有延长的 治疗 窗口、冷藏稳定性和节省剂量的给药,突出了细胞、宿主 导向的持久呼吸道 抗病毒药物 防御的途径。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为开发一种新型 宿主 定向疗法提供了信息,该疗法可以针对季节性和高致病性流感病毒株提供广泛的保护,特别是在弱势群体中,对 监测、治疗 和预防策略具有潜在影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究是在小鼠模型中进行的,可能无法完全转化为人类;局限性包括缺乏人体数据以及需要进一步评估不同人群的长期安全性和有效性。

analysis_zh.methods: 通过 DLS、zeta 电位和 HPLC 评估 NanoSTING 稳定性;单次鼻内给药后评估药代动力学(PK)、药效学(PD)和安全性;通过 qPCR 分析鼻/肺组织中的 IFN 基因(Ifnb1 和 Cxcl10),并通过 H&E 分析安全性。
analysis_zh.main_results: NanoSTING 在 4°C 下稳定 12 个月,封装的 cGAMP 没有损失;单次鼻内剂量在鼻和肺组织中诱导出强大的 Ifnb1 和 Cxcl10,而没有组织学损伤;在甲型/H1N1 和乙型流感攻击模型中,一剂 NanoSTING 减少了体重减轻,加速了恢复,并且优于十剂奥司他韦。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,单剂量鼻内 NanoSTING 可激活保护性 I 型 IFN 程序,并为 A/B 型流感(包括 H5N1)提供广泛的治疗益处,具有延长的 治疗 窗口、冷藏稳定性和节省剂量的给药,突出了细胞、宿主 导向的持久呼吸道 抗病毒药物 防御的途径。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为开发一种新型 宿主 定向疗法提供了信息,该疗法可以针对季节性和高致病性流感病毒株提供广泛的保护,特别是在弱势群体中,对 监测、治疗 和预防策略具有潜在影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究是在小鼠模型中进行的,可能无法完全转化为人类;局限性包括缺乏人体数据以及需要进一步评估不同人群的长期安全性和有效性。

title: Subtype-specific neutralizing antibodies promote antigenic shift during influenza virus co-infection.
abstract: Reassortment between different influenza strains occurs when they co-infect the same host cell. The emergence of a reassortant virus depends on both its intrinsic fitness and extrinsic factors, including preexisting humoral immunity. The generation of pandemic strains, such as H2N2 and H3N2, and zoonotic influenza A viruses, such as H5N6, H5N8, and H7N9, in birds is suggested to be the result of extensive selection by preexisting antibodies. To further explore the role of humoral immunity in reassortment, we generated two divergent fluorescent protein-expressing viruses and used strain-specific and cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) to assess the impact of cross-immunity on reassortment. Our results indicate that all mAbs altered the genotypic diversity and significantly reduced the release of progeny virions in co-infected cells both in vitro and in vivo . Moreover, antibody transfer studies in mice revealed protection from challenge with divergent pathogenicity profiles. Notably, selection driven by a strain-specific mAb depended on its neutralizing specificity, whereas the selection driven by broadly reactive mAbs was independent of neutralization specificity. Our findings demonstrate that preexisting neutralizing antibodies shape reassortment and that strain-specific neutralizing antibodies promote antigenic shift during co-infection, which is not the case for broadly cross-reactive antibodies that recognize influenza viruses from different subtypes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of humoral immunity in influenza virus reassortment, particularly how preexisting antibodies influence the emergence of reassortant viruses with pandemic or zoonotic potential.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used fluorescent protein-expressing viruses and monoclonal antibodies in co-infected cells, both in vitro and in vivo, to assess the impact of cross-immunity on reassortment.
analysis.methods: Divergent fluorescent protein-expressing viruses were generated, and strain-specific and cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies were used to evaluate their effects on genotypic diversity and progeny virion release during co-infection.
analysis.main_results: All monoclonal antibodies altered genotypic diversity and significantly reduced progeny virion release in co-infected cells both in vitro and in vivo; antibody transfer in mice provided protection against divergent pathogenicity profiles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that preexisting neutralizing antibodies shape reassortment, with strain-specific antibodies promoting antigenic shift during co-infection, unlike broadly cross-reactive antibodies that recognize different subtypes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance and prevention strategies by highlighting how preexisting immunity can influence influenza virus evolution and the emergence of pandemic or zoonotic strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relied on in vitro and in vivo models with monoclonal antibodies, which may not fully replicate natural infection dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how humoral immunity influences influenza virus reassortment, a key mechanism for pandemic and zoonotic strain emergence. Using fluorescent protein-expressing viruses and monoclonal antibodies, the researchers found that all antibodies reduced progeny virion release and altered genotypic diversity in co-infected cells. Strain-specific antibodies promoted antigenic shift, while broadly cross-reactive antibodies did not. These findings demonstrate that preexisting immunity shapes viral evolution, with implications for surveillance and prevention strategies targeting influenza reassortment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨体液免疫在流感病毒重配中的作用,特别是先前存在的抗体如何影响具有大流行或人畜共患潜力的重配病毒的出现。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在体外和体内的共感染细胞中使用了表达荧光蛋白的病毒和单克隆抗体,以评估交叉免疫对重配的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 产生了表达不同荧光蛋白的病毒,并使用毒株特异性和交叉反应性单克隆抗体来评估它们在共感染期间对基因型多样性和子代病毒粒子释放的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有单克隆抗体都改变了基因型多样性,并在体外和体内显着减少了共感染细胞中子代病毒粒子的释放;小鼠体内的抗体转移提供了针对不同致病性特征的保护。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,预先存在的中和抗体形成重配,与识别不同亚型的广泛交叉反应抗体不同,菌株特异性抗体在共感染期间促进抗原转变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了预先存在的免疫力如何影响流感病毒 进化 以及大流行或人畜共患毒株的出现,为 进化 和预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究依赖于单克隆抗体的体外和体内模型,可能无法完全复制自然感染动态。

abstract_zh: 当不同流感毒株共同感染相同的 宿主 细胞时,就会发生不同流感毒株之间的重配。重配病毒的出现取决于其内在适应性和外在因素,包括预先存在的体液免疫。鸟类中 H2N2 和 H3N2 等大流行毒株以及 H5N6、H5N8 和 H7N9 等人畜共患甲型流感病毒的产生被认为是先前存在的抗体广泛选择的结果。为了进一步探讨体液免疫在重配中的作用,我们生成了两种不同的表达荧光蛋白的病毒,并使用毒株特异性和交叉反应性单克隆抗体(mAb)来评估交叉免疫对重配的影响。我们的结果表明,所有单克隆抗体都改变了基因型多样性,并在体外和体内显着减少了共感染细胞中子代病毒粒子的释放。此外,小鼠体内的抗体转移研究揭示了针对不同致病性特征的攻击的保护作用。值得注意的是,菌株特异性 mAb 驱动的选择取决于其中和特异性,而广泛反应性 mAb 驱动的选择则独立于中和特异性。我们的研究结果表明,预先存在的中和抗体会形成重配,并且毒株特异性中和抗体会在共感染期间促进抗原转变,而识别不同亚型流感病毒的广泛交叉反应抗体则并非如此。

title: A Multidonor Plasma Antibody Class with Broad Activity Against H5N1 Neuraminidase 2309455
abstract: Abstract Introduction Highly pathogenic H5N1 influenza viruses remain a significant pandemic threat, underscoring the need to define antibody responses that target conserved viral epitopes. Here, we characterize a panel of plasma IgG—derived human neuraminidase (NA)—specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) that share a convergent CDR-H3 “DR motif,” previously implicated in substrate mimicry at the NA active site. Methods Using IgG proteomics discovery, ELISA, immunofluorescence assays, enzymatic inhibition, and microneutralization assays, we show that multiple DR-motif mAbs bind H5N1 NA with high potency and directly inhibit NA activity. Results Several antibodies exhibit cross-reactivity with divergent influenza A strains and target overlapping epitopes within the NA catalytic site. Importantly, two DR-motif mAbs (41508 and 125308) confer protection in C57BL/6 mice against lethal challenge with A/Texas/37/2024 (H5N1; clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13). Conclusion Together, these data define a multidonor class of circulating, functional human NA-directed antibodies with broad antiviral activity and highlight the NA active site as an accessible and vulnerable target for next-generation influenza vaccines and antibody-based countermeasures. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

abstract_original: Abstract Introduction Highly pathogenic H5N1 influenza viruses remain a significant pandemic threat, underscoring the need to define antibody responses that target conserved viral epitopes. Here, we characterize a panel of plasma IgG—derived human neuraminidase (NA)—specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) that share a convergent CDR-H3 “DR motif,” previously implicated in substrate mimicry at the NA active site. Methods Using IgG proteomics discovery, ELISA, immunofluorescence assays, enzymatic inhibition, and microneutralization assays, we show that multiple DR-motif mAbs bind H5N1 NA with high potency and directly inhibit NA activity. Results Several antibodies exhibit cross-reactivity with divergent influenza A strains and target overlapping epitopes within the NA catalytic site. Importantly, two DR-motif mAbs (41508 and 125308) confer protection in C57BL/6 mice against lethal challenge with A/Texas/37/2024 (H5N1; clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13). Conclusion Together, these data define a multidonor class of circulating, functional human NA-directed antibodies with broad antiviral activity and highlight the NA active site as an accessible and vulnerable target for next-generation influenza vaccines and antibody-based countermeasures. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

title: Development and Analytical Validation of a Multiplex Real-Time RT-PCR Assay for Simultaneous Detection of Avian Influenza A Virus and Newcastle Disease Virus
abstract: Avian influenza A virus (AIV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV) are among the most damaging pathogens of poultry, and AIV also carries zoonotic potential that places it within the One Health agenda. The two infections frequently produce overlapping clinical signs, so a method that detects both in a single reaction has clear practical value for surveillance. We developed a duplex one-step real-time reverse-transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) that detects AIV in the FAM channel and NDV in the ROX channel. Primers and hydrolysis probes were designed against conserved regions of the AIV nucleoprotein and matrix genes and the NDV matrix, phosphoprotein and nucleoprotein genes, after alignment of 500 sequences per virus retrieved from GenBank from different geographic regions. Annealing temperature, primer and probe concentrations were optimised, and recombinant plasmids carrying the target fragments served both as positive controls and as quantitative standards. The assay was specific for AIV and NDV, with no cross-reactivity with infectious bronchitis virus and no signal crossover between channels; its analytical sensitivity reached approximately 10–20 RNA copies per reaction. Qualitative results on reference isolates were fully concordant with two commercial veterinary kits (Cohen’s κ = 1.00), and the assay passed inter-laboratory commission testing. This study establishes the design and core analytical performance of a laboratory-developed duplex assay; expanded in silico inclusivity on contemporary sequences, a broader specificity panel, inhibitor-containing matrices, an internal amplification control, and prospective clinical validation are required before routine surveillance deployment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 A 病毒 (AIV) 和新城疫病毒 (NDV) 是对家禽最具破坏性的病原体之一,AIV 还具有人畜共患病的潜力,因此将其纳入“同一个健康”议程。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一种双重一步式实时逆转录 PCR (RT-qPCR) 检测方法,用于同时检测 AIV 和 NDV。
elements_zh.methods: 在对来自 GenBank 的每种病毒 500 个序列进行比对后,针对 AIV 核蛋白和基质基因以及 NDV 基质、磷蛋白和核蛋白基因的保守区域设计引物和水解探针;优化退火温度、引物和探针浓度,并以重组质粒作为阳性对照和定量标准品。
elements_zh.main_results: 该检测对 AIV 和 NDV 具有特异性,与传染性支气管炎病毒无交叉反应,通道间无信号交叉;其分析灵敏度达到每个反应约 10-20 个 RNA 拷贝,参考分离株的定性结果与两种商业兽医试剂盒完全一致(Cohen's κ = 1.00)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究确定了实验室开发的同时检测 AIV 和 NDV 的双重检测的设计和核心分析性能。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 由于家禽中 AIV 和 NDV 感染的临床症状重叠,双重检测对于 监测 具有明显的实用价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在常规 监测 部署之前,需要扩大当代序列的计算机包容性、更广泛的特异性组、包含抑制剂的基质、内部扩增控制和前瞻性临床验证;由于需要进一步验证,证据强度中等。

title_zh: 用于同时检测 禽流感 A 病毒和新城疫病毒的多重实时 RT-PCR 检测的开发和分析验证
source_body_en: Avian influenza A virus (AIV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV) are among the most damaging pathogens of poultry, and AIV also carries zoonotic potential that places it within the One Health agenda. The two infections frequently produce overlapping clinical signs, so a method that detects both in a single reaction has clear practical value for surveillance. We developed a duplex one-step real-time reverse-transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) that detects AIV in the FAM channel and NDV in the ROX channel. Primers and hydrolysis probes were designed against conserved regions of the AIV nucleoprotein and matrix genes and the NDV matrix, phosphoprotein and nucleoprotein genes, after alignment of 500 sequences per virus retrieved from GenBank from different geographic regions. Annealing temperature, primer and probe concentrations were optimised, and recombinant plasmids carrying the target fragments served both as positive controls and as quantitative standards. The assay was specific for AIV and NDV, with no cross-reactivity with infectious bronchitis virus and no signal crossover between channels; its analytical sensitivity reached approximately 10–20 RNA copies per reaction. Qualitative results on reference isolates were fully concordant with two commercial veterinary kits (Cohen’s κ = 1.00), and the assay passed inter-laboratory commission testing. This study establishes the design and core analytical performance of a laboratory-developed duplex assay; expanded in silico inclusivity on contemporary sequences, a broader specificity panel, inhibitor-containing matrices, an internal amplification control, and prospective clinical validation are required before routine surveillance deployment.
abstract_zh: 禽流感 A 病毒 (AIV) 和新城疫病毒 (NDV) 是对家禽最具破坏性的病原体之一,AIV 还具有人畜共患病的潜力,因此将其纳入“同一个健康”议程。这两种感染经常产生重叠的临床症状,因此在单一反应中检测这两种感染的方法对于 监测 具有明显的实用价值。我们开发了一种双工一步式实时逆转录 PCR (RT-qPCR),可检测 FAM 通道中的 AIV 和 ROX 通道中的 NDV。对从不同地理区域的 GenBank 检索到的每种病毒的 500 个序列进行比对后,针对 AIV 核蛋白和基质基因以及 NDV 基质、磷蛋白和核蛋白基因的保守区域设计引物和水解探针。退火温度、引物和探针浓度均经过优化,携带目标片段的重组质粒既可作为阳性对照,又可作为定量标准品。该检测对 AIV 和 NDV 具有特异性,与传染性支气管炎病毒无交叉反应,通道间无信号交叉;其分析灵敏度达到每个反应约 10-20 个 RNA 拷贝。参考分离株的定性结果与两种商业兽医试剂盒完全一致(Cohen’s κ = 1.00),并且该测定通过了实验室间委员会测试。这项研究确立了实验室开发的双工检测的设计和核心分析性能;在常规 监测 部署之前,需要在计算机上扩展当代序列的包容性、更广泛的特异性面板、包含抑制剂的基质、内部扩增控制和前瞻性临床验证。

title: Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) as a method for detecting avian influenza virus in field conditions (review)
abstract: Currently, the avian influenza virus continues to pose a global biological threat, affecting populations of wild and domestic birds, as well as mammals (including humans). Circulating strains of the virus have a negative impact not only on natural ecosystems but also on the economic sustainability of the agro-industrial sector. The constant genetic variability of the virus requires effective, fast, and reliable laboratory diagnostic tools. Despite its high accuracy, the "gold standard" of diagnostics—polymerase chain reaction (PCR)—has limited applicability both in laboratories with limited resource equipment and in field conditions due to the need for complex equipment and high qualification of personnel. The presented review examines loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) as a promising alternative for avian influenza virus monitoring both in laboratories with a limited resource base and in field conditions. The specified method allows amplification of nucleic acids at a constant temperature (60–65 °C), ensuring high speed of analysis (15–40 minutes), sensitivity, and specificity. A key advantage is the possibility of visual interpretation of the results using colorimetric indicators, which minimizes equipment requirements. Special attention is paid to modern modifications: RT-LAMP for work with RNA, multiplex formats, and integration with microchip platforms. Practical validation of the method confirms its analytical characteristics, comparable to RT-PCR, and effectiveness in monitoring studies. Thus, LAMP represents a technologically mature tool for rapid screening, capable of increasing the effectiveness of epizootiological surveillance. For its widespread implementation, standardization of protocols and their integration into official guidelines for veterinary control are necessary.

title: Estimating the infection fatality ratio of zoonotic avian influenza viruses with pandemic potential using an evolutionary epidemiological model
abstract: The risk of zoonotic avian influenza (AIV) infection to humans is challenging to estimate as many human avian influenza virus infections are undetected because infections may be asymptomatic, symptomatic but not tested, and difficult to identify through contact tracing, as human-to-human transmission is rare. We derive equations that consider the evolutionary mechanisms that give rise to pandemics and are parameterized to be consistent with records of past pandemics. We estimate that thousands of human infections with AIVs possessing pandemic potential occur worldwide in an average year. Combining these estimates with H5N1 fatality data, we estimate a historical average infection fatality ratio of 32 (95% uncertainty interval: 9.6-75) deaths per 10,000 infections. This estimate is comparable to SARS-CoV-2 during the recent pandemic and higher than seasonal human influenza. We estimate that preventing animal-to-human influenza spillovers would delay pandemic emergence by several years. Preventing human infections with AIVs is necessary given the high risk of severe outcomes to individuals and to reduce the risk of pandemics occurring in the future.

title: Genetic determinants of cell- and egg-preferred replication in H3N2 canine influenza virus.
abstract: The H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV), which originated from avian influenza viruses and has circulated in dogs for over two decades, remains poorly understood in terms of its host adaptation mechanisms and cellular tropism. In this study, we isolated two phenotypically distinct H3N2 CIV strains (CX3 and CX12) from a canine respiratory disease outbreak. Although both were isolated using MDCK cells, CX3 showed higher replication efficiency and plaque-forming ability in MDCK cells, whereas CX12 replicated more efficiently in chicken embryos. Using reverse genetics, we identified the PB1 gene as a critical enhancer of viral polymerase activity and the HA gene as a key contributor to viral stability, both of which collectively mediate cell-preferred replication. These findings provide mechanistic insights into H3N2 CIV host adaptation and offer a foundation for future vaccine development.

title_zh: H3N2 犬流感病毒细胞和卵优先复制的遗传决定因素。
source_body_en: The H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV), which originated from avian influenza viruses and has circulated in dogs for over two decades, remains poorly understood in terms of its host adaptation mechanisms and cellular tropism. In this study, we isolated two phenotypically distinct H3N2 CIV strains (CX3 and CX12) from a canine respiratory disease outbreak. Although both were isolated using MDCK cells, CX3 showed higher replication efficiency and plaque-forming ability in MDCK cells, whereas CX12 replicated more efficiently in chicken embryos. Using reverse genetics, we identified the PB1 gene as a critical enhancer of viral polymerase activity and the HA gene as a key contributor to viral stability, both of which collectively mediate cell-preferred replication. These findings provide mechanistic insights into H3N2 CIV host adaptation and offer a foundation for future vaccine development.

title: The One Health Blind Spot at the Human‒Animal Interface in US Influenza Surveillance.
abstract: Novel influenza A viruses have cost thousands of lives and billions of dollars of economic losses in the 21st century, and 2 of the past 4 pandemic influenza A viruses likely originated in animal populations on the North American continent. Despite this, the human and veterinary influenza surveillance systems in the United States are poorly connected and have fallen short of congressional mandates for data sharing and interoperability. This places the United States in a reactive posture that is focused on containment of outbreaks that have already occurred rather than proactive surveillance and prevention. The significant investments in surveillance infrastructure and genomic technologies spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic, along with the new National One Health Framework, present a unique opportunity to modernize influenza surveillance with a greater emphasis on the interconnectedness of human and animal health. However, funding for enhanced surveillance is set to decrease significantly as pandemic-era funding sunsets. Continuing investments into novel surveillance technologies have been critical in addressing the recent H5N1 influenza outbreaks and will be critical to prevent future economic losses and losses of both human and animal life. ( Am J Public Health . 2026;116(8):1220-1228. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308445).

title: Feasibility of studying respiratory infection transmission in a Swiss household cohort: Findings from the BEready ("Bern, get ready") study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the need for pandemic preparedness, including the establishment of cohorts allowing for the rapid collection of data and biological specimens. We investigated the feasibility of performing self-sampling for respiratory viruses, online questionnaires and telemedicine in the "Bern, get ready" (BEready) household-based cohort in Switzerland. METHODS: In this pilot study, we enrolled 108 households: 161 adults, 32 children, 29 cats and 15 dogs. We instructed participants to collect a nasal swab if they experienced symptoms of a respiratory infection. Household members of index cases collected swabs, including from their pets, a week later to identify secondary cases. Samples were tested for 13 respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, RSV and rhinovirus, using a commercially available multiplex PCR. RESULTS: From 26/05/2023 to 16/09/2024, 78 households reported 152 disease events. We obtained valid results from 131/188 (70%) expected samples from index cases, 105/152 (69%) from household contacts, and 24/47 (51%) from pets. The positivity rate of the swabs was 82/131 (63%) among index cases and 24/105 (23%) among human household contacts. CONCLUSIONS: Decentralized respiratory virus surveillance was feasible in our household-based cohort. Our study will inform the investigation of future emerging diseases, such as an H5N1 pandemic.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

title: Long-term milk-yield impact and recovery in HPAI-affected cows across consecutive lactations and its association with antibody response.
abstract: This cohort study quantifies the long-term impact of HPAI H5N1 on cumulative milk yield and milk-yield trajectories during the affected lactation, and carryover effects in the subsequent lactation; and evaluates the relationship between antibody response and affected status under field conditions. A cohort of 1,845 lactating Holstein cows from a commercial dairy herd affected by HPAI H5N1 was monitored across current and subsequent lactations. HPAI affected status was defined as ≥ 30% decline in daily milk yield relative to a 7-d baseline. Milk yield trajectories were analyzed using generalized additive mixed models with spline-based smooth terms for time, including a random intercept for cow and fixed effects for parity, stage of lactation, and HPAI affected status. Associations between antibody response and affected status were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression models, adjusted for parity and stage of lactation. Affected animals (n = 772) had an average cumulative milk loss of 9.6% (1,109 kg) per 305 d, representing an average loss of $569 per affected cow. Higher losses occurred in multiparous (-12.4%) than primiparous cows (-3.9%). Retention into the subsequent lactation was similar between affected and unaffected cows (69.8% vs. 69.2%, respectively), and no evidence of carryover effects was detected. Based on post-outbreak serologic testing (n = 121), multiparous cows had higher odds of testing ELISA-positive for antibodies to HPAI than primiparous cows (OR = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.07-6.28). The adjusted predicted proportions of cows classified as affected based on the milk-yield decline criterion during the HPAI outbreak were 63.2% among ELISA-positive cows, 42.1% among ELISA-suspect cows, and 33.2% among ELISA-negative cows. ELISA-positive cows had higher odds of experiencing severe milk-yield decline than ELISA-negative cows (OR = 3.45, 95% CI:1.44-8.69). Cows with stronger antibody response had higher odds of being classified as affected based on the milk-yield decline (OR = 0.51 per 0.05 S/N increase; 95% CI:0.35-0.75). Overall, cows affected during the HPAI outbreak had substantial milk-yield and economic losses during the affected lactation. Limited recovery was most evident among multiparous cows and among cows affected in early lactation, regardless of parity. No evidence of carryover effects was observed in the subsequent lactation. Stronger post-outbreak antibody responses were associated with affected status during the outbreak, defined by milk-yield decline as a clinically relevant sign.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在量化 HPAI H5N1 对连续哺乳期产奶量和恢复的长期影响,并评估现场条件下抗体反应与受影响状态之间的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 队列研究 中受 HPAI H5N1 感染的商业奶牛群中的 1,845 头哺乳期荷斯坦奶牛进行了当前和后续哺乳期的监测。
elements_zh.methods: HPAI 受影响状态定义为每日产奶量相对 7 天基线下降 ≥ 30%。使用广义加法混合模型和基于样条的平滑时间项来分析产奶量轨迹,包括奶牛的随机截距和胎次、泌乳阶段和 HPAI 影响状态的固定效应。使用多变量逻辑和线性回归模型评估抗体反应和受影响状态之间的关联,并根据胎次和哺乳阶段进行调整。
elements_zh.main_results: 受影响的动物 (n = 772) 每 305 天平均累积产奶损失为 9.6% (1,109 公斤),每头受影响的奶牛平均损失 569 美元。经产奶牛 (-12.4%) 的损失率高于初产奶牛 (-3.9%)。受影响奶牛和未受影响奶牛的后续泌乳保留率相似(分别为 69.8% 和 69.2%),没有证据表明存在残留效应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,暴发 后更强的抗体反应与 暴发 期间受影响的状态相关,将产奶量下降定义为临床相关体征。新颖之处在于量化受 HPAI 影响的奶牛在连续哺乳期的长期产奶量影响和恢复模式。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为奶牛群中高致病性禽流感的 监测 和经济影响评估提供了信息,强调了巨大的经济负担和有限的恢复,特别是在多产奶牛中。这支持有针对性的干预措施,以减轻 暴发 期间的损失。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个商业奶牛群,可能会降低普遍性。尽管如此,由于样本量大、纵向设计和稳健的统计方法,证据强度很高。

title: First report of human infection caused by swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v virus in mainland China: a confirmed case identified through influenza-like illness surveillance, Kunming (Yunnan), 2025
abstract: Objective This case report details the epidemiological characteristics of the first human case of swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v infection identified in mainland China, to formulate guidelines for the prevention and control of human swine-origin influenza A (H1N2) virus infections. Methods Clinical and epidemiological data of the case were collected through field epidemiological investigation combined with laboratory testing. Specimens were collected from the patient, close contacts, animals subjects (including one deceased pig), and environmental matrices and analyzed to trace the potential infection source and characterize the clinical and epidemiological features. Results This study describes a sporadic, isolated case of human infection with swine influenza A(H1N2)v in mainland China, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission. Prior to symptom onset, the patient inhabited a high-risk mixed residential setting with frequent close exposure to domestic livestock and poultry. Specially, his townhouse stood adjacent to his great-uncle’s residence, where swine were raised; the great-uncle also documented the mortality of one pig. But had no contact with human confirmed cases presenting similar clinical manifestations. Testing of the collected specimens confirmed influenza N2 subtype positivity in lung tissue specimens obtained from the deceased pigs, whereas all remaining animal and environmental specimens yielded negative test results. The patient was eventually discharged after clinical recovery. A total of 30 close contacts completed self-health monitoring and throat swab screening. title: Analysis of Influenza A viruses using the resonant recognition model
abstract: Bird flu (Avian influenza) and human flu are both caused by Influenza A viruses, but they differ significantly in their host adaptation, transmission and severity. Here, we have used the Resonant Recognition Model (RRM), which is innovative approach using knowledge from quantum physics, biochemistry and mathematics, capable to analyse interactions between proteins and their targets, including other proteins, DNA, RNA, or small molecules. Using the RRM model we have identified different characteristics for different types of flu viruses, and we have found that there are three groups of flu viruses with completely different interactions with host cells receptors. Such finding can provide explanation why different flu viruses can interact only with specific hosts and why there is extremely low cross infection between different species, in particular between birds and humans.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research Archive

title: Integrating in silico Humanization and DNA Delivery to engineer anti-Influenza Monoclonal Antibodies for improved in vivo expression 2267274
abstract: Abstract Introduction Highly pathogenic avian influenzas (HPAI) of the H5 subtype represent an ongoing zoonotic threat to human and animal health. Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) offer a powerful tool for pandemic preparedness, yet translation to the clinic often requires humanization to avoid immune reactions against murine antibodies, often impacting its function across divergent viral strains. Methods We developed a computational pipeline integrating BioPhi with in-house refinement to generate humanized variants of 5C2, a murine antibody elicited against a clade 2.3.2.1 H5N1 virus. To assess whether humanized antibodies could retain the breadth and potency of the parental clone, we designed a panel of unique humanized constructs and compared them to a VH/VL chimera and the murine wild-type mAb, which were all genetically optimized for in vivo expression. Results We confirmed in vitro expression of all constructs and subsequently delivered them as DNA-encoded monoclonal antibody (DMAbs) via injection and in vivo electroporation (EP) to wild-type mice. Sera from DMAb treated mice exhibited strong binding and pseudovirus neutralization to multiple H5N1 clades, including the currently circulating panzootic clade 2.3.4.4b virus. In vivo DMAb delivery supported sustained expression across constructs for several months. Conclusion These data demonstrate that optimized in silico humanization can preserve key functional properties, including cross-reactivity against multiple clades. Our results support the use of this computational workflow for rapid generation of humanized antibodies with broad activity, highlighting its potential application against emerging seasonal or pandemic threats. Funding Source NIH/NIAID CIVICs (75N93019C00051) Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5 viruses pose an ongoing zoonotic threat to human and animal health, creating a need for broadly protective countermeasures that can be rapidly deployed during emerging outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study engineered humanized variants of a murine anti-H5 monoclonal antibody (5C2) using a computational pipeline and assessed their expression and function in vivo after DNA delivery to wild-type mice.
analysis.methods: A computational pipeline integrating BioPhi with in-house refinement generated humanized variants of the murine 5C2 antibody, which were then optimized for in vivo expression and delivered as DNA-encoded monoclonal antibodies (DMAbs) via injection and in vivo electroporation to mice.
analysis.main_results: Sera from DMAb-treated mice showed strong binding and pseudovirus neutralization against multiple H5N1 clades, including the currently circulating clade 2.3.4.4b virus, and sustained antibody expression was observed across constructs for several months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that optimized in silico humanization preserved key functional properties, including cross-reactivity against divergent H5N1 clades, and that the computational workflow enables rapid generation of humanized antibodies with broad activity against emerging threats.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the potential of DNA-encoded humanized antibodies as a platform for pandemic preparedness, enabling rapid response to seasonal or pandemic influenza threats through sustained, cross-reactive immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro binding and pseudovirus neutralization assays and in vivo expression in mice, leaving uncertainty about clinical efficacy, safety, and performance against diverse circulating strains in humans.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the zoonotic risk posed by highly pathogenic avian influenza H5 viruses by engineering humanized monoclonal antibodies to preserve cross-clade reactivity and in vivo expression. Using a computational pipeline, the authors humanized a murine anti-H5 antibody (5C2) and delivered DNA-encoded versions (DMAbs) to mice via electroporation. Sera from treated mice demonstrated strong binding and neutralization against multiple H5N1 clades, including clade 2.3.4.4b, with sustained expression over months. The authors interpret these results as evidence that optimized humanization can maintain functional breadth, supporting the workflow’s potential for rapid pandemic preparedness. While promising, the findings are preclinical, relying on mouse models and in vitro assays, and their clinical relevance remains untested.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5 viruses pose an ongoing zoonotic threat to human and animal health, creating a need for broadly protective countermeasures that can be rapidly deployed during emerging outbreaks.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study engineered humanized variants of a murine anti-H5 monoclonal antibody (5C2) using a computational pipeline and assessed their expression and function in vivo after DNA delivery to wild-type mice.
analysis_en.methods: A computational pipeline integrating BioPhi with in-house refinement generated humanized variants of the murine 5C2 antibody, which were then optimized for in vivo expression and delivered as DNA-encoded monoclonal antibodies (DMAbs) via injection and in vivo electroporation to mice.
analysis_en.main_results: Sera from DMAb-treated mice showed strong binding and pseudovirus neutralization against multiple H5N1 clades, including the currently circulating clade 2.3.4.4b virus, and sustained antibody expression was observed across constructs for several months.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that optimized in silico humanization preserved key functional properties, including cross-reactivity against divergent H5N1 clades, and that the computational workflow enables rapid generation of humanized antibodies with broad activity against emerging threats.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the potential of DNA-encoded humanized antibodies as a platform for pandemic preparedness, enabling rapid response to seasonal or pandemic influenza threats through sustained, cross-reactive immunity.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro binding and pseudovirus neutralization assays and in vivo expression in mice, leaving uncertainty about clinical efficacy, safety, and performance against diverse circulating strains in humans.

title_zh: 整合计算机人源化和 DNA 递送来设计抗流感单克隆抗体,以改善体内表达 2267274
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Highly pathogenic avian influenzas (HPAI) of the H5 subtype represent an ongoing zoonotic threat to human and animal health. Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) offer a powerful tool for pandemic preparedness, yet translation to the clinic often requires humanization to avoid immune reactions against murine antibodies, often impacting its function across divergent viral strains. Methods We developed a computational pipeline integrating BioPhi with in-house refinement to generate humanized variants of 5C2, a murine antibody elicited against a clade 2.3.2.1 H5N1 virus. To assess whether humanized antibodies could retain the breadth and potency of the parental clone, we designed a panel of unique humanized constructs and compared them to a VH/VL chimera and the murine wild-type mAb, which were all genetically optimized for in vivo expression. Results We confirmed in vitro expression of all constructs and subsequently delivered them as DNA-encoded monoclonal antibody (DMAbs) via injection and in vivo electroporation (EP) to wild-type mice. Sera from DMAb treated mice exhibited strong binding and pseudovirus neutralization to multiple H5N1 clades, including the currently circulating panzootic clade 2.3.4.4b virus. In vivo DMAb delivery supported sustained expression across constructs for several months. Conclusion These data demonstrate that optimized in silico humanization can preserve key functional properties, including cross-reactivity against multiple clades. Our results support the use of this computational workflow for rapid generation of humanized antibodies with broad activity, highlighting its potential application against emerging seasonal or pandemic threats. Funding Source NIH/NIAID CIVICs (75N93019C00051) Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

title: Impact of Non‐Pharmaceutical Interventions Targeted at COVID‐19 Pandemic on Influenza Burden—A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Seasonal influenza imposes a substantial global health burden. The COVID‐19 pandemic, accompanied by widespread non‐pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), profoundly disrupted respiratory virus circulation, offering a unique opportunity to assess their broader epidemiological impact. This study aimed to quantify changes in influenza burden between the pre‐pandemic and intra‐pandemic periods. Within the RESPINOW project, we conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting absolute influenza case counts before and during the pandemic were included. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using a modified NHLBI tool for before–after studies. Influenza cases were normalized by reporting period length, and relative changes were estimated using incidence rate ratios. Subgroup analyses explored age, setting, hemisphere, human development index, influenza transmission zones, WHO regions, and viral strains. Of 20,676 screened records, 115 studies from 98 countries were included. Globally, influenza incidence declined by −92% (95% CI: −94 to −90) following the onset of the pandemic. Reductions varied geographically, ranging from near‐elimination in several countries to more modest declines (e.g., South Korea: −61%, 95% CI: −79 to −26). Decreases were observed across all transmission zones and WHO regions, with descriptively larger reductions observed in high‐income countries (−96%, 95% CI: −98 to −94) than in low‐income settings (−82%, 95% CI: −88 to −73). title: Intranasal administration of a pan-reactive influenza antibody reveals Fc-independent mode of protection 2259232
abstract: Abstract Introduction Monoclonal antibodies protect through two core mechanisms: their antigen-binding fragment (Fab) directly binds and neutralizes viral antigens, while the fragment crystallizable domain (Fc) engages Fcγ receptors to activate immune effector functions. We investigated and segregated the relative contribution of each antibody domain to immune protection by comparing peripheral/systemic versus local/mucosal delivery within a mouse model of antibody prophylaxis against influenza virus Methods We performed intranasal versus intravenous delivery of CR9114, the broadest known human influenza antibody, which engages a conserved epitope on the hemagglutinin stem to provide protection against both influenza A and influenza B viruses within pre-clinical challenge models. Mice received either wild-type CR9114, Fc-silenced mutants (LALA, N297Q), or the bivalent antigen-binding F(ab’)2 fragment alone (no Fc domain) 24 hours before lethal challenge with influenza A/H1N1, A/H3N2, A/H5N1, B/Yamagata, or B/Victoria viruses. Survival and weight change were measured to determine protection and median effective doses (ED50). Results Intranasal delivery of CR9114 resulted in an increase in potency against lethal influenza A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yam and B/Vic compared to intravenous administration, up to 50-fold. Systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, whereas intranasal protection remained strong even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats. The F(ab’)2 fragment alone conferred full prophylaxis when delivered locally but was ineffective systemically. Conclusion These findings reveal that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection. Local mucosal delivery achieves potent Fc-independent immunity, which was also seen in the absence of conventional neutralization activity, offering a new strategy for antibody-based prevention of influenza and other respiratory infections. Funding Source Leyden Laboratories B.V. Topic Categories Mucosal and Regional Immunology (MUC)

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a mouse model of antibody prophylaxis against influenza virus, comparing intranasal versus intravenous delivery of the broadest known human influenza antibody CR9114 against multiple influenza strains.
analysis.methods: Mice received wild-type CR9114, Fc-silenced mutants (LALA, N297Q), or the bivalent antigen-binding F(ab’)2 fragment alone 24 hours before lethal challenge with influenza A/H1N1, A/H3N2, A/H5N1, B/Yamagata, or B/Victoria viruses; survival and weight change were measured to determine protection and median effective doses (ED50).
analysis.main_results: Intranasal delivery of CR9114 resulted in an increase in potency against lethal influenza A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yamagata, and B/Victoria compared to intravenous administration, up to 50-fold; systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, whereas intranasal protection remained strong even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relative contribution of antibody domains to immune protection against influenza virus by comparing intranasal versus intravenous delivery of the broad-spectrum antibody CR9114 in mice. Results showed that intranasal delivery significantly increased potency against multiple influenza strains, including A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yamagata, and B/Victoria, compared to intravenous administration. Systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, but intranasal protection remained effective even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats, including the F(ab’)2 fragment alone. These findings demonstrate that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection, with local mucosal delivery achieving potent Fc-independent immunity, offering a novel strategy for preventing influenza and other respiratory infections.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过比较小鼠模型中的外周/全身与局部/粘膜递送,研究和分离抗体结构域对流感病毒免疫保护的相对贡献。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate and segregate the relative contribution of antibody domains to immune protection against influenza virus by comparing peripheral/systemic versus local/mucosal delivery in a mouse model.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a mouse model of antibody prophylaxis against influenza virus, comparing intranasal versus intravenous delivery of the broadest known human influenza antibody CR9114 against multiple influenza strains.
analysis_en.methods: Mice received wild-type CR9114, Fc-silenced mutants (LALA, N297Q), or the bivalent antigen-binding F(ab’)2 fragment alone 24 hours before lethal challenge with influenza A/H1N1, A/H3N2, A/H5N1, B/Yamagata, or B/Victoria viruses; survival and weight change were measured to determine protection and median effective doses (ED50).
analysis_en.main_results: Intranasal delivery of CR9114 resulted in an increase in potency against lethal influenza A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yamagata, and B/Victoria compared to intravenous administration, up to 50-fold; systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, whereas intranasal protection remained strong even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection, with local mucosal delivery achieving potent Fc-independent immunity even in the absence of conventional neutralization activity.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Local mucosal delivery offers a new strategy for antibody-based prevention of influenza and other respiratory infections, potentially enhancing protection against diverse strains including avian influenza A/H5N1.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on pre-clinical challenge models in mice, and while the findings are robust within this context, further studies are needed to confirm efficacy in humans; the evidence strength is moderate due to the limited translational scope.

title_zh: 鼻内施用泛反应性流感抗体揭示了 Fc 独立的保护模式 2259232
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Monoclonal antibodies protect through two core mechanisms: their antigen-binding fragment (Fab) directly binds and neutralizes viral antigens, while the fragment crystallizable domain (Fc) engages Fcγ receptors to activate immune effector functions. We investigated and segregated the relative contribution of each antibody domain to immune protection by comparing peripheral/systemic versus local/mucosal delivery within a mouse model of antibody prophylaxis against influenza virus Methods We performed intranasal versus intravenous delivery of CR9114, the broadest known human influenza antibody, which engages a conserved epitope on the hemagglutinin stem to provide protection against both influenza A and influenza B viruses within pre-clinical challenge models. Mice received either wild-type CR9114, Fc-silenced mutants (LALA, N297Q), or the bivalent antigen-binding F(ab’)2 fragment alone (no Fc domain) 24 hours before lethal challenge with influenza A/H1N1, A/H3N2, A/H5N1, B/Yamagata, or B/Victoria viruses. Survival and weight change were measured to determine protection and median effective doses (ED50). Results Intranasal delivery of CR9114 resulted in an increase in potency against lethal influenza A/H1N1, A/H5N1, A/H3N2, B/Yam and B/Vic compared to intravenous administration, up to 50-fold. Systemic protection required an intact Fc domain, whereas intranasal protection remained strong even with Fc-silenced or Fc-depleted formats. The F(ab’)2 fragment alone conferred full prophylaxis when delivered locally but was ineffective systemically. Conclusion These findings reveal that the route of antibody delivery determines its mechanism of protection. Local mucosal delivery achieves potent Fc-independent immunity, which was also seen in the absence of conventional neutralization activity, offering a new strategy for antibody-based prevention of influenza and other respiratory infections. Funding Source Leyden Laboratories B.V. Topic Categories Mucosal and Regional Immunology (MUC)
abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 单克隆抗体通过两个核心机制提供保护:其抗原结合片段 (Fab) 直接结合并中和病毒抗原,而片段可结晶结构域 (Fc) 与 Fcγ 受体结合以激活免疫效应功能。我们通过比较针对流感病毒的抗体预防小鼠模型中的外周/全身与局部/粘膜递送,研究并分离了每个抗体结构域对免疫保护的相对贡献。方法我们进行了CR9114的鼻内与静脉内递送,CR9114是已知最广泛的人类流感抗体,其与血凝素茎上的保守表位结合,以在临床前挑战模型中提供针对甲型流感和乙型流感病毒的保护。在用 A/H1N1、A/H3N2、A/H5N1、B/Yamagata 或 B/Victoria 病毒致死攻击前 24 小时,小鼠接受野生型 CR9114、Fc 沉默突变体(LALA、N297Q)或单独的二价抗原结合 F(ab’)2 片段(无 Fc 结构域)。测量存活率和体重变化以确定保护作用和中位有效剂量 (ED50)。结果 与静脉内给药相比,鼻内给药 CR9114 的抗致命性流感 A/H1N1、A/H5N1、A/H3N2、B/Yam 和 B/Vic 的效力提高了 50 倍。全身保护需要完整的 Fc 结构域,而即使采用 Fc 沉默或 Fc 耗尽的形式,鼻内保护仍然很强。当局部递送时,单独的 F(ab’)2 片段可以提供充分的预防作用,但全身无效。结论这些发现揭示了抗体递送途径决定了其保护机制。局部粘膜递送实现了有效的不依赖于 Fc 的免疫,这在缺乏常规中和活性的情况下也可见到,为基于抗体的流感和其他呼吸道感染的预防提供了新策略。资金来源 Leyden Laboratories B.V. 主题类别 粘膜和区域免疫学 (MUC)

title: Optimizing T Cell Priming Using TLR4/9 Combination Adjuvant For Robust Cell-Mediated Immunity Against Influenza 2307646
abstract: Abstract Introduction Subunit vaccines are safe but rarely induce robust, long-lasting immunity, especially cell-mediated immunity (CMI). Here, we investigated the potential of IVAX-1, a combination of TLR4 (MPLA) and TLR9 (CpG 1018) agonists formulated in a squalene oil-in-water emulsion (AddaVax), to mediate protection and generate CMI. Methods We leveraged a murine H5N1 influenza model with fate-map reporters, conditional knock-out mice, multiphoton imaging, and flow cytometry to elucidate early spatiotemporal features of IVAX-1-driven immunity. Antigen-specific CMI was evaluated via ELISpot and recall assays. Results Immune priming with IVAX-1 enhanced dendritic cell (DC) maturation and recruitment of myeloid cells to the injection site, resulting in higher numbers of neutrophils, monocytes, and antigen-presenting DCs in the draining lymph node (DLN), independent of antigen clearance kinetics. This induced islands of IFN-γ+ cells in the DLN, suggesting clonal expansion. In addition, IVAX-1 generated a robust antigen-specific functional (IFN-γ+) T cell response. Deletion of Type 1 conventional DCs (XCR1+) cells abrogated IVAX-1-mediated T cell response. Furthermore, immunization with IVAX-1 generated significantly higher numbers of flu-specific memory T cells in the lungs and spleen. IVAX-1 conferred durable protection and superior viral clearance from the lungs up to 60 days after immunization. Conclusion By leveraging synergistic innate immune activation through multiple TLR pathways, the combination optimizes T cell priming without relying on antigen depot effects. Our findings identify key early innate immune events and cellular mediators that drive robust CMI and demonstrate the potential of TLR agonist combinations to elicit durable T-cell immunity. Funding Source NIH/NIAID grants U01AI160397 & R01AI168063; Adjuvant Comparison and Characterization contract BAA-DAIT-75N93020R00022; and grant from the Defense Threat Reduction Agency #HDTRA-18-1-0036; UC Irvine UROP Research Experience Fellowship; NIH-MARC U-STAR trai Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

title_zh: 使用 TLR4/9 组合佐剂优化 T 细胞启动,以实现强大的细胞介导的流感免疫 2307646
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Subunit vaccines are safe but rarely induce robust, long-lasting immunity, especially cell-mediated immunity (CMI). Here, we investigated the potential of IVAX-1, a combination of TLR4 (MPLA) and TLR9 (CpG 1018) agonists formulated in a squalene oil-in-water emulsion (AddaVax), to mediate protection and generate CMI. Methods We leveraged a murine H5N1 influenza model with fate-map reporters, conditional knock-out mice, multiphoton imaging, and flow cytometry to elucidate early spatiotemporal features of IVAX-1-driven immunity. Antigen-specific CMI was evaluated via ELISpot and recall assays. Results Immune priming with IVAX-1 enhanced dendritic cell (DC) maturation and recruitment of myeloid cells to the injection site, resulting in higher numbers of neutrophils, monocytes, and antigen-presenting DCs in the draining lymph node (DLN), independent of antigen clearance kinetics. This induced islands of IFN-γ+ cells in the DLN, suggesting clonal expansion. In addition, IVAX-1 generated a robust antigen-specific functional (IFN-γ+) T cell response. Deletion of Type 1 conventional DCs (XCR1+) cells abrogated IVAX-1-mediated T cell response. Furthermore, immunization with IVAX-1 generated significantly higher numbers of flu-specific memory T cells in the lungs and spleen. IVAX-1 conferred durable protection and superior viral clearance from the lungs up to 60 days after immunization. Conclusion By leveraging synergistic innate immune activation through multiple TLR pathways, the combination optimizes T cell priming without relying on antigen depot effects. Our findings identify key early innate immune events and cellular mediators that drive robust CMI and demonstrate the potential of TLR agonist combinations to elicit durable T-cell immunity. title: Contribution of Influenza H5 Head and Stalk Domains to the Development of Functional Non-Neutralizing Antibodies Following Mucosal rH5-NE Vaccination 2333118
abstract: Abstract Introduction In a prior Phase 1 trial we showed that an intranasal (IN) recombinant hemagglutinin (HA) H5 vaccine (rH5; A/Indo/05) nanoemulsion-adjuvanted (rH5 NE) and given on days 1 and 29 effectively primed the immune system. Participants received rH5 NE (25—100 μg; IN; n = 24), unadjuvanted rH5 (100 μg; IN; n = 7), or placebo (n = 6). Only rH5 NE recipients exhibited significant increases in HAI titers after a heterologous intramuscular (IM) H5N1 booster on day 197, confirming successful mucosal priming. Anti-H5 antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity also demonstrated this priming effect. Here, we evaluated whether rH5 NE elicited cross reactive ADCC and antibody-dependent cell phagocytosis (ADCP) responses to diverse H5 HAs and examined contributions of HA head and stalk domains. Methods Plasma from days 1, 57, and 225 was analyzed. ADCC was assessed using beads coated with whole, head only, or stalk only H5 HAs incubated with plasma and exposed to a CD16a expressing reporter cell line. ADCP was quantified by THP 1 uptake of antigen-coated AF488—beads. ADCC seroconversion was defined as a ≥ 4 fold increase; ADCP seroconversion as a ≥ 2 fold increase. Results By day 57, 33% (8/24) rH5 NE recipients showed ADCC seroconversion to A/Indo/05 whole HA, rising to 50% after the day-197 IM boost. Unadjuvanted rH5 and placebos seroconverted only after boosting (4/7=57% & 4/6=67%, respectively). Similar trends were seen for A/Viet/04 and A/cow Tx/24. Head specific ADCC seroconversion in rH5 NE reached 46% (11/24) at day 57 and 88% (21/24) at day 225, whereas unadjuvanted rH5 responded only at day 225 (4/7=57%). Placebos showed no responses. Stalk specific ADCC was largely preexisting across all groups, with minimal vaccine induced increases. ADCP trends mirrored ADCC findings. Conclusion Intranasal rH5 NE induces cross reactive ADCC and ADCP responses driven primarily by antibodies targeting the H5-head, supporting its capacity to induce effective mucosal priming. Funding Source Support from the following Grants: NIH U01AI148081, BlueWillow Contract, lead author is a UMB-ITP-Vax scholar (NIH R25AI175011), Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the contribution of influenza H5 head and stalk domains to functional non-neutralizing antibodies following mucosal rH5-NE vaccination. In a Phase 1 trial, participants received intranasal rH5 NE (25–100 μg; n=24), unadjuvanted rH5 (100 μg; n=7), or placebo (n=6). The vaccine induced cross-reactive ADCC and ADCP responses, primarily driven by antibodies targeting the H5-head domain. By day 57, 33% of rH5 NE recipients showed ADCC seroconversion, increasing to 50% after an intramuscular boost. Head-specific responses reached 88% by day 225, while stalk-specific responses were largely preexisting. The findings support the vaccine's capacity for effective mucosal priming against diverse H5 viruses.

title_zh: 流感 H5 头和茎结构域对粘膜 rH5-NE 疫苗接种 2333118 后功能性非中和抗体开发的贡献
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction In a prior Phase 1 trial we showed that an intranasal (IN) recombinant hemagglutinin (HA) H5 vaccine (rH5; A/Indo/05) nanoemulsion-adjuvanted (rH5 NE) and given on days 1 and 29 effectively primed the immune system. Participants received rH5 NE (25—100 μg; IN; n = 24), unadjuvanted rH5 (100 μg; IN; n = 7), or placebo (n = 6). Only rH5 NE recipients exhibited significant increases in HAI titers after a heterologous intramuscular (IM) H5N1 booster on day 197, confirming successful mucosal priming. Anti-H5 antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity also demonstrated this priming effect. Here, we evaluated whether rH5 NE elicited cross reactive ADCC and antibody-dependent cell phagocytosis (ADCP) responses to diverse H5 HAs and examined contributions of HA head and stalk domains. Methods Plasma from days 1, 57, and 225 was analyzed. ADCC was assessed using beads coated with whole, head only, or stalk only H5 HAs incubated with plasma and exposed to a CD16a expressing reporter cell line. ADCP was quantified by THP 1 uptake of antigen-coated AF488—beads. ADCC seroconversion was defined as a ≥ 4 fold increase; ADCP seroconversion as a ≥ 2 fold increase. Results By day 57, 33% (8/24) rH5 NE recipients showed ADCC seroconversion to A/Indo/05 whole HA, rising to 50% after the day-197 IM boost. Unadjuvanted rH5 and placebos seroconverted only after boosting (4/7=57% & 4/6=67%, respectively). Similar trends were seen for A/Viet/04 and A/cow Tx/24. Head specific ADCC seroconversion in rH5 NE reached 46% (11/24) at day 57 and 88% (21/24) at day 225, whereas unadjuvanted rH5 responded only at day 225 (4/7=57%). Placebos showed no responses. Stalk specific ADCC was largely preexisting across all groups, with minimal vaccine induced increases. ADCP trends mirrored ADCC findings. Conclusion Intranasal rH5 NE induces cross reactive ADCC and ADCP responses driven primarily by antibodies targeting the H5-head, supporting its capacity to induce effective mucosal priming. Funding Source Support from the following Grants: NIH U01AI148081, BlueWillow Contract, lead author is a UMB-ITP-Vax scholar (NIH R25AI175011), Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

title: Self-Reported Vaccination Coverage and Occupational Immunization Gaps Among Veterinarians in Málaga, Spain: A One Health Perspective
abstract: Veterinarians are routinely exposed to occupational infectious hazards at the human–animal interface, making vaccination an important preventive measure within a One Health framework. However, evidence on vaccination coverage and immunization practices in this professional group remains limited. This study assessed self-reported vaccination coverage, attitudes toward vaccination, perceived barriers, and training needs among registered veterinarians in Málaga, Spain. A cross-sectional anonymous survey was distributed to all actively practicing veterinarians registered with the Official Veterinary Association of Málaga. The questionnaire collected sociodemographic and professional information, self-reported vaccination status, attitudes toward vaccination, and perceived training needs. A total of 164 veterinarians participated (response rate: 15.2%). Given the voluntary nature of participation, findings should be interpreted as descriptive. Vaccination coverage was low for several vaccines relevant to occupational or adult immunization, including seasonal influenza (21.3%), rabies (23.2%), and tetanus–diphtheria–pertussis boosters (47.3%). Nearly half of respondents (49.1%) were uncertain about their hepatitis B vaccination status. In contrast, COVID-19 vaccination uptake was high (96.9% received at least one dose). Although most participants considered vaccination highly important, self-reported coverage remained limited for several recommended vaccines. Qualitative responses identified barriers related to access to vaccination, information, and the absence of structured occupational vaccination programmes. Among the surveyed veterinarians in Málaga, these findings support the need for clearer occupational vaccination recommendations, improved access to immunization services, and enhanced vaccinology training. Such measures could strengthen occupational health protection and support One Health prevention strategies at the human–animal interface.

title: Local immune networks promote respiratory IgA responses after mucosal vaccination 2260370
abstract: Abstract Introduction Mucosal immunization and respiratory IgA offer significant promise in protecting against airborne pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2. However, the conditions and mechanisms that lead to the robust induction of respiratory IgA responses following mucosal vaccination remain poorly understood. Methods In this project, we established SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection and mucosal adenovirus-based booster vaccination models. Using genetic mouse models and various in vivo and in vitro blockade or depletion approaches, we further investigated the mechanisms regulating respiratory IgA responses. Results Here we found that a mucosal adenovirus-based booster vaccination in mouse models revealed that respiratory booster immunization elicited markedly stronger and more durable respiratory IgA, T cell response, and protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2, supporting the promise of respiratory mucosal vaccination. Mechanistically, we identified that local CD4+ T cells support respiratory IgA production by promoting IgA+ B cell class switching, proliferation, and survival in situ. This T cell help depended on interactions between local Blimp-1+ T-bet+ Th1 cells and B cells, mediated through ICOS/CD40L/MHC-II engagement and IL-21 signaling. Furthermore, lung macrophages contributed to the mucosal IgA response via TGF-β production. Consequently, mucosal administration of SARS-CoV-2 Spike-encoding mRNA encapsulated in pulmonary surfactant (PS)- incorporated lipid nanoparticles designed to target lung macrophages elicited a stronger mucosal IgA response. Conclusion Our results uncover a local cellular network supporting enhanced mucosal IgA responses, with implications for the development of optimal mucosal immunization strategies against SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory pathogens such as H5N1 influenza. Funding Source AI147394, AG069264, AI112844, HL170961, AI154598, AI176171 to J.S., AI67986, AI177467 to Hui.H; U54CA260582 to S.L.L; R01AI168684 to G. Z.; S.L.L was also supported by a fund provided by an anonymous private donor to The Ohio State University. Topic Categories Mucosal and Regional Immunology (MUC)

title_zh: 局部免疫网络促进粘膜后呼吸道 IgA 反应 疫苗接种 2260370
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Mucosal immunization and respiratory IgA offer significant promise in protecting against airborne pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2. However, the conditions and mechanisms that lead to the robust induction of respiratory IgA responses following mucosal vaccination remain poorly understood. Methods In this project, we established SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection and mucosal adenovirus-based booster vaccination models. Using genetic mouse models and various in vivo and in vitro blockade or depletion approaches, we further investigated the mechanisms regulating respiratory IgA responses. Results Here we found that a mucosal adenovirus-based booster vaccination in mouse models revealed that respiratory booster immunization elicited markedly stronger and more durable respiratory IgA, T cell response, and protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2, supporting the promise of respiratory mucosal vaccination. Mechanistically, we identified that local CD4+ T cells support respiratory IgA production by promoting IgA+ B cell class switching, proliferation, and survival in situ. This T cell help depended on interactions between local Blimp-1+ T-bet+ Th1 cells and B cells, mediated through ICOS/CD40L/MHC-II engagement and IL-21 signaling. Furthermore, lung macrophages contributed to the mucosal IgA response via TGF-β production. Consequently, mucosal administration of SARS-CoV-2 Spike-encoding mRNA encapsulated in pulmonary surfactant (PS)- incorporated lipid nanoparticles designed to target lung macrophages elicited a stronger mucosal IgA response. Conclusion Our results uncover a local cellular network supporting enhanced mucosal IgA responses, with implications for the development of optimal mucosal immunization strategies against SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory pathogens such as H5N1 influenza. title: Evaluating AlphaFold 3 immune complex structure prediction and cryo-EM analysis of broadly neutralizing antibodies towards influenza hemagglutinin 2309571
abstract: Abstract Introduction Epitope:paratope interactions define the breadth and affinity an antibody has towards an antigen. Computational structure prediction can help to model immune complexes as a method of in silico screening for broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs). However, we do not currently understand how structural predictions and confidence metrics correlate with experimental data. Here, we evaluate the accuracy of AlphaFold 3 (AF3) in predicting immune complexes of a known class of bnAbs towards a conserved epitope on influenza hemagglutinin (HA). Methods We used single-cell RNA sequencing to generate a library of HA reactive, paired antibody sequences. AF3 was used to computationally model antibody-HA interactions. Antibodies were expressed and characterized with BLI, ELISA, and microneutralization assays. Negative stain electron microscopy (nsEM) and single particle cryo-electron microscopy (SPA cryo-EM) were used to structurally characterize immune complexes. Results B cell receptor sequencing of PBMCs from 23 healthy, human donors generated 1161 H5 HA-specific, paired antibody sequences. These sequences comprised new examples within a known class of antibodies (VH1-69, of which previous examples are in the AF3 training set) likely to target the conserved central stem. We modeled these antibody sequences in complex with H1N1 and H5N1 HAs using AF3. Highly confident predictions correlated with antibodies possessing high affinity and breadth. Moreover, in silico epitope footprints strongly matched experimental nsEM data. Finally, we resolved atomistic details with high-resolution SPA cryo-EM that explain challenges with AF3 immune complex prediction. Conclusion AF3 can be used to screen for VH1-69 bnAbs targeting a conserved epitope on influenza HA with high confidence. This method of down selection may be applied to other classes of antibodies and to other epitopes. However, models still need to be tuned to accurately predict immune complexes of novel or less characterized antibody classes. Funding Source Endowed Fellowship in the Skaggs Graduate School of Chemical and Biological Sciences, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). Topic Categories Computational and Systems Immunology (COMP)

Here, we evaluate the accuracy of AlphaFold 3 (AF3) in predicting immune complexes of a known class of bnAbs towards a conserved epitope on influenza hemagglutinin (HA). Methods We used single-cell RNA sequencing to generate a library of HA reactive, paired antibody sequences. AF3 was used to computationally model antibody-HA interactions. Antibodies were expressed and characterized with BLI, ELISA, and microneutralization assays. Negative stain electron microscopy (nsEM) and single particle cryo-electron microscopy (SPA cryo-EM) were used to structurally characterize immune complexes. Results B cell receptor sequencing of PBMCs from 23 healthy, human donors generated 1161 H5 HA-specific, paired antibody sequences. These sequences comprised new examples within a known class of antibodies (VH1-69, of which previous examples are in the AF3 training set) likely to target the conserved central stem. We modeled these antibody sequences in complex with H1N1 and H5N1 HAs using AF3. Highly confident predictions correlated with antibodies possessing high affinity and breadth. Moreover, in silico epitope footprints strongly matched experimental nsEM data. Finally, we resolved atomistic details with high-resolution SPA cryo-EM that explain challenges with AF3 immune complex prediction. Conclusion AF3 can be used to screen for VH1-69 bnAbs targeting a conserved epitope on influenza HA with high confidence. This method of down selection may be applied to other classes of antibodies and to other epitopes. However, models still need to be tuned to accurately predict immune complexes of novel or less characterized antibody classes. title: Immunization with deglycosylated H7N9 VLP enhances cross-strain protective antibody responses against avian influenza H7N9 variants in mice
abstract: Introduction The rapidly evolving avian influenza H7N9 virus remains a threaten to public health globally. There is an urgent need to develop broad-spectrum vaccines capable of eliciting functional cross-strain protective immunity against emerging viral variants. Methods N-linked glycosylation can shield critical residues from immune recognition. Here, a prototype virus-like particle (VLP) was constructed based on the antigenic sequences derived from A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus. Glycosidase enzymes were utilized to trim the glycan molecules for generating monoglycosylated VLP (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated VLP (VLPng) derivates. The structural integrity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity of these VLPs were systematically evaluated. Results Both VLPmg and VLPng maintained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity like the fully glycosylated prototype VLP (VLPfg). Immunization with deglycosylated VLPs induced robust virus-specific antibodies and a balanced Th1/Th2 immune profile in mice, whereas the titers were comparable to that of VLPfg. Among them, VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 virus strains, indicating improved cross-strain reactive antibody responses. Conclusion This study demonstrated the enzymatic deglycosylation of influenza H7N9 VLP improves the induction of broadly protective antibody responses in mice. The nonglycosylated H7N9 VLP represents a potential vaccine candidate to against the threat of antigenically divergent H7N9 virus variants.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether enzymatic deglycosylation of H7N9 virus-like particles (VLPs) could enhance cross-strain protective antibody responses. Prototype VLPs derived from A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 were enzymatically modified to produce monoglycosylated and nonglycosylated derivatives. In mice, both modified VLPs retained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity comparable to the fully glycosylated prototype. Immunization with the nonglycosylated VLP (VLPng) induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against multiple H7N9 strains than the monoglycosylated or fully glycosylated VLPs. The authors interpret these results as evidence that deglycosylation improves the breadth of protective immunity. The study concludes that VLPng represents a potential vaccine candidate against antigenically divergent H7N9 variants. However, the findings are limited to mouse models and require human validation.

abstract_zh: 简介 快速进化的 禽流感 H7N9 病毒仍然对全球公共卫生构成威胁。迫切需要开发广谱 疫苗,能够引发针对新出现的病毒变种的功能性跨毒株保护性免疫。方法 N-连接糖基化可以保护关键残基免受免疫识别。在这里,基于 A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 病毒的抗原序列构建了原型病毒样颗粒 (VLP)。利用糖苷酶修剪聚糖分子,以生成单糖基化 VLP (VLPmg) 和非糖基化 VLP (VLPng) 衍生物。对这些 VLP 的结构完整性、抗原性和免疫原性进行了系统评估。结果 VLPmg 和 VLPng 均保持与完全糖基化原型 VLP (VLPfg) 一样的血凝活性和抗原性。用去糖基化的 VLP 进行免疫可以在小鼠体内诱导出强大的病毒特异性抗体和平衡的 Th1/Th2 免疫特征,而滴度与 VLPfg 相当。其中,VLPng针对不同的H7N9病毒株诱导了更高的血凝抑制和中和抗体滴度,表明跨病毒株反应性抗体反应得到改善。结论 这项研究表明,流感 H7N9 VLP 的酶促去糖基化可改善小鼠体内广泛保护性抗体反应的诱导。非糖基化的 H7N9 VLP 代表了潜在的 疫苗 候选药物,可对抗抗原不同的 H7N9 病毒变种的威胁。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 H7N9 构成持续的公共卫生威胁,现有的 疫苗 可能无法针对抗原不同的变种提供足够的跨毒株保护。该研究解决了对能够引发功能性交叉菌株免疫的广谱 疫苗 的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究根据A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9病毒的抗原序列构建了病毒样颗粒(VLP),并在小鼠中评估了其结构完整性、抗原性和免疫原性。
analysis_zh.methods: N-连接糖基化经过酶促修饰,生成单糖基化 (VLPmg) 和非糖基化 (VLPng) VLP,然后评估其血凝活性、抗原性和免疫原性。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于小鼠模型,研究结果需要在人体中进行验证,以在临床转化之前评估安全性、免疫原性和有效性。

title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 A/H9N2 造成持续的人畜共患病和兽医威胁,但用于 抗病毒药物 化合物优先级排序的有效计算工具仍然不发达,特别是在高维神经筛选中的​​优化器行为方面。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究提出牛顿差分(NDD)优化作为一种​​针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的新型优化器,目的是评估其在对齐的分子指纹表示和化学结构验证协议中的性能。
elements_zh.methods: 由 615 种候选活性化合物和 844 种诱饵组成的 1,459 个分子的对齐基准由 EState(79 个特征)、PubChem(881 个特征)和 Klekota–Roth(4,860 个特征)指纹代表,共享相同的分子身份、标签和分割分配。固定多层感知器 (MLP) 分类器使用 NDD 和七个基线优化器在分层、支架键和相似性聚类分割协议下跨五个重复种子进行训练。
elements_zh.main_results: NDD 在支架关键和相似性聚类协议下在 Klekota–Roth 指纹上实现了最高的描述性 ROC-AUC 和 PR-AUC,并且在分层分割下保持竞争力,ROC-AUC 为 0.9872。架构敏感性测试证实了跨多种网络配置的稳定 NDD 性能,ROC-AUC 值范围为 0.9876 至 0.9890。与无 Hessian 优化相比,在相同的仅 CPU 配置下,NDD 将 Klekota-Roth 上的每次运行时间从大约 50-54 秒减少到大约 8 秒,同时实现了相当的排名性能。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这项工作的新颖性在于首次对 H9N2 神经虚拟筛选的 NDD 进行系统评估,证明正对角线曲率感知缩放在基于稀疏高维配体的筛选设置中提供了实用、稳定且计算高效的优化替代方案。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的 抗病毒药物 化合物优先排序提供了一种计算有效的优化策略,这可以加速针对这种人畜共患威胁的潜在治疗方法的发现。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在实施实际的 抗病毒药物 优先级排序之前,外部验证和前瞻性实验确认仍然是必要的。由于研究的计算性质和实验验证的需要,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 禽流感 A/H9N2 造成持续的人畜共患病和兽医威胁,但用于 抗病毒药物 化合物优先级排序的有效计算工具仍然不发达,特别是在高维神经筛选中的​​优化器行为方面。本研究提出了牛顿除差(NDD)优化,这是一种轻量级正对角曲率感知训练策略,作为针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的新型优化器,目的是评估其在对齐的分子指纹表示和化学结构验证协议中的性能。由 615 种候选活性化合物和 844 种诱饵组成的 1,459 个分子的对齐基准由 EState(79 个特征)、PubChem(881 个特征)和 Klekota–Roth(4,860 个特征)指纹代表,共享相同的分子身份、标签和分割分配。固定多层感知器 (MLP) 分类器使用 NDD 和七个基线优化器在分层、支架键和相似性聚类分割协议下跨五个重复种子进行训练。NDD 在支架密钥和相似性聚类协议下的 Klekota–Roth 指纹上实现了最高的描述性 ROC-AUC(接收者操作特征 - 曲线下面积)和 PR-AUC(曲线下精确召回面积),并且在分层分割下保持竞争力,ROC-AUC 为 0.9872。架构敏感性测试证实了跨多种网络配置的稳定 NDD 性能,ROC-AUC 值范围为 0.9876 至 0.9890。与无 Hessian 优化相比,在相同的仅 CPU 配置下,NDD 将 Klekota-Roth 上的每次运行时间从大约 50-54 秒减少到大约 8 秒,同时实现了相当的排名性能。这项工作的新颖性在于首次系统评估 H9N2 神经虚拟筛选的 NDD,证明正对角线曲率感知缩放在稀疏高维配体筛选设置中提供了实用、稳定且计算高效的优化替代方案,尽管在实际 抗病毒药物 优先级排序之前仍然需要外部验证和前瞻性实验确认。
